title: Token SLI sampling, histogram buckets, and multi-region failover playbook
creator: Leila Park
description:
Goal: Provide a repeatable instrumentation and dashboard buildout that (1) captures token-level latency SLIs with statistically-sound sampling and histogram buckets, (2) attributes tail latency to region/shard/model/version, and (3) operationalizes circuit breaker thresholds and multi-region failover decisions via dashboards and an actionable playbook.

Background: We currently emit request-level latency and coarse token counters. This obscures generation tail behavior and makes region failover tuning guesswork. The new work will add per-token timing markers, sampling rules for high-volume routes, histogram-based SLIs (percentiles + burn rate style SLOs), and Grafana dashboards + alerting tied to failover/circuit rules.

Scope: Instrument runtime (C++/Rust service) to emit the following metrics:
- runtime.token_latency_histogram (Prometheus histogram with exemplar tracing) labelled by: model, model_variant, region, shard_id, route, prefix_token_count, generation_token_count, cache_hit (yes/no), batch_size_bucket
- runtime.token_latency_count (counter) and runtime.token_latency_sum (for summary fallback)
- runtime.kv_cache_hit_ratio (labelled by model, region, shard)
- runtime.batch_composition_gauge (distribution of batch sizes per second)
- runtime.circuit_breaker_state (enum gauge) and runtime.circuit_breaker_trigger_reason (label)

Design decisions:
- Use Prometheus histograms with exponential buckets tuned for short/medium/long tokens (buckets: 1ms..5s). We'll prototype with buckets: [1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096] ms then iterate.
- Sampling: Full capture for P0 routes and 1/10 sampling for high-volume internal tooling routes. Sampling metadata must be emitted so dashboards can re-scale counts.
- Attribution: Add trace id exemplars to histogram buckets for 95/99/99.9 percentile debugging (Link traces in Jaeger).
- Separation of token types: emit separate metrics for prefix vs generation tokens so SLOs reflect generation cost, not user-upload parsing.
- Storage/retention: Store histograms at 1m resolution for 90 days, rollup to 5m for 365 days.

Dashboard buildout: create three Grafana pages in the runtime -> reliability folder:
1) Token Latency Overview: 50/95/99/99.9 for generation tokens, per-model quick filters, bucketed heatmap over time.
2) Failover & Circuit Map: regional ingress rates, per-region 99p token latency, circuit breaker states, active fallbacks, and a region-to-region failover heatmap (showing frequency and duration of fallovers).
3) SLO Telemetry & Regression: burn-rate view for SLO windows, recent commits affecting SLO, links to canary cohorts and eval-run diffs.

Alerts and playbook:
- P0 alert if regional 99p generation token latency exceeds X ms (configurable) for 5m AND token error-rate > 0.2% -> immediate oncall paging.
- P1 alert if overall cluster 99p exceeds warning threshold for 15m -> email + Slack.
- Automated circuit break: sliding window algorithm that considers token-units-per-second + 99p latency; when triggered, circuit moves to TRIPPED for region and automatically routes traffic to fallback regions/model-quantized variants. Circuit triggers should be visible in dashboard with last-trigger reason and exemplar trace.
- Playbook steps: verify metric, check KV cache hit ratio and batch composition, examine exemplar traces, roll back recent model rollouts, optional manual failover (steps + RBAC link).

Implementation plan / milestones:
1) Prototype: add histogram metric and exemplar to a single low-risk internal route, create local dashboard panel. (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1623)
2) Expand: instrument top 8 customer-facing routes with sampling and labels; add cache hit metrics. (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1637)
3) Dashboards: create Grafana panels, templating for model/region; wire alerts. (dashboards/grafana/ID: 98421 token-latency-overview)
4) Runbook: publish Confluence playbook and run a runbook dry-run in the next Chaos Tuesday. (confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Token+SLI+Playbook)
5) Rollout: staged enable across regions with canary (5%) -> 25% -> 100% over two weeks.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for metric emitter and histogram bucket correctness.
- Synthetic generator to produce controlled token-latency distributions (three profiles: nominal, taily, kv-cache-degraded) used in CI to validate dashboard panels and alert thresholds.
- Post-rollout validation: compare pre/post SLO burn rate for 48h.

Risks & mitigations:
- High cardinality explosion: mitigate via label cardinality caps (max 6 shards in label, coalesce model_variant tags into "quantized"/"full_precision" for high-cardinality models).
- Cost increase from exemplars/traces: only add exemplars for top-10 offending buckets and sampled requests.
- Alert fatigue: tune P1/P0 thresholds in Stage 2 using historical 99p distributions.

Success criteria:
- Dashboards show reliable 99p and 99.9p generation token values per-region.
- Circuit breaker triggers reflected in dashboard with <2min lag.
- Operations can perform manual or automated failover using documented playbook steps and recover SLOs within target RTO for prod incidents.

Outputs / artifacts: PR links, Grafana IDs, Confluence page, and a test harness repo. See comments for artifact links.

Next steps: unblock PR review, schedule runtime infra change window, and book Chaos Tuesday dry-run.
